content.overview: Hiba is an immediate inter vivos gift under Muslim law. The three classical essentials are declaration by a competent donor, acceptance by the donee, and delivery of possession (actual or constructive). Musha (gift of an undivided share) and marz-ul-maut (death-bed gift) are special problems. Hiba is distinct from wasiyat (will).
content.glance: Ask: (1) Declaration? (2) Acceptance? (3) Delivery of possession? (4) Musha or marz-ul-maut issues?
content.study:
Without delivery of possession the third essential fails. Musha gifts of divisible property may be irregular unless possession is given as the law accepts. Marz-ul-maut gifts are limited and may take effect only to the extent of the testamentary third if the conditions of death-illness are met.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Three essentials
sections.body: Declaration by competent donor; acceptance by donee; delivery of possession (actual or constructive).

sections.heading: Immediate transfer
sections.body: Intention must be immediate inter vivos transfer, not a disposition operating only on death.

sections.heading: Musha
sections.body: Gift of an undivided share; divisible vs indivisible property; possession requirements.

sections.heading: Marz-ul-maut
sections.body: Death-bed gift specially limited; may be restricted to the testamentary third if conditions are met.

sections.heading: Hiba vs wasiyat
sections.body: Hiba is immediate; wasiyat operates on death and is generally limited to one-third for non-heirs without consent.

examples.title: Valid hiba
examples.body: Donor declares gift of a house, donee accepts, possession is handed over — valid hiba.

hypotheticals.question: Is a registered gift deed without possession a complete hiba?
hypotheticals.analysis: Delivery of possession is a classical essential; registration alone does not necessarily complete the hiba under Muslim law.

distinctions.title: Hiba vs wasiyat
distinctions.right: Disposition operating on death; generally limited to one-third for non-heirs without consent.

misconceptions.trap: A registered gift deed without possession is always a complete hiba.
misconceptions.correction: Delivery of possession is a classical essential under Muslim law.
